title: Data Versioning
shortDefinition: The practice of systematically tracking and managing changes to datasets used for AI model training.
definition: Data versioning is the practice of systematically tracking and managing changes to datasets used for AI model training — recording exactly which version of data was used to train each model version, enabling reproducible training, diagnosing why model performance changed between versions, and rolling back to earlier data states when needed. Without data versioning, determining whether a model performance change was caused by a code change, a hyperparameter change, or a data change is often impossible after the fact — frustratingly common when debugging production model degradation.

sections.title: Why data versioning is separate from model versioning
sections.description: Model versioning tracks the trained model; data versioning tracks the underlying datasets used to train it.

content.text: Model versioning tracks the trained model artifact and its associated metadata. Data versioning tracks the underlying datasets — which records were included, what preprocessing was applied, and how the data changed between training runs. Both are necessary for full reproducibility: knowing which model version is deployed tells you nothing about whether a performance change was caused by changed training data if that data wasn't versioned alongside the model. The two work together: a complete audit trail of model performance requires knowing both the exact model version and the exact data version it was trained on.

items: Model versioning — tracks model artifacts and metadata.
Data versioning — tracks datasets and preprocessing changes.
Full reproducibility — requires both model and data versioning.
Audit trail — complete history of what trained each model.
Diagnostic value — enables root cause analysis of performance changes.

sections.title: The reproducibility gap in many AI projects

content.text: A surprisingly common situation: a model is retrained with updated data and performance degrades, but there's no systematic record of what changed in the training data between versions — only the inference that 'something in the data changed.' Without data versioning, diagnosing the specific data change responsible for the degradation requires manual investigation that may not be possible if the earlier data state wasn't preserved. Data versioning, combined with model versioning, transforms this investigation from guesswork into a systematic comparison between specific, documented versions.

items: Common situation — retrained model degrades without clear cause.
No record — what changed in the data is unknown.
Manual investigation — may be impossible without preserved state.
Systematic comparison — versioning enables documented comparison.
Diagnostic transformation — from guesswork to precise analysis.

sections.title: Limitations and risks of data versioning

content.text: Data versioning has limitations. It requires discipline to maintain and can add storage overhead, especially for large datasets. Retroactive versioning is not possible for historical data that wasn't saved. Versioning can be complex for streaming data or rapidly changing sources. Data subject deletion rights (GDPR) can complicate versioning if personally identifiable information is involved. The tooling is less mature than code versioning, and teams may need training to use versioning effectively. Versioning doesn't guarantee data quality — only tracking.

items: Discipline required — requires consistent usage to be valuable.
Storage overhead — versioning adds storage costs.
Retroactive impossible — historical data can't be versioned.
Streaming complexity — challenging for rapidly changing data.
Privacy considerations — GDPR adds complexity with PII.
Tooling maturity — less mature than code versioning.

content.text: Data versioning enables reproducibility but requires discipline and investment. Start early — you can't version data retroactively.

content.title: Key metric
content.text: Measure model reproducibility success rate — can you reproduce any previous model version with exactly the same data and code? 100% is the goal.

faqs.title: Frequently asked questions about data versioning

items.question: What's the difference between data versioning and database backup?
items.answer: Backup preserves data for recovery from failure; versioning specifically tracks what changed between versions with enough metadata to reproduce training exactly or diagnose differences — a more structured, ML-specific discipline.

items.question: How does data versioning help when a model's performance unexpectedly degrades?
items.answer: By enabling direct comparison between the data used in the last good model version and the data used in the degraded version, identifying exactly what changed in the training data — rather than knowing only that something changed.

items.question: What tools does ClickMasters use for data versioning?
items.answer: DVC (Data Version Control) is commonly used for ML dataset versioning, integrated with Git for code versioning and MLflow for model versioning to create a complete, unified audit trail.

items.question: How does data versioning interact with GDPR and data deletion requirements?
items.answer: This is a genuine consideration — versioning systems need to be designed to accommodate data subject deletion rights without losing the ability to reproduce earlier model training; ClickMasters scopes this during implementation planning.

items.question: How long does implementing data versioning take?
items.answer: 6–16 weeks depending on whether it's standalone data versioning or integrated with model versioning for full MLOps reproducibility.

items.question: Should we implement data versioning from the beginning, or is it something we can add later?
items.answer: Earlier is better — adding versioning retroactively can't recover the historical record that was never captured, meaning the diagnostic value only begins from when versioning is implemented.

items.question: What is DVC (Data Version Control)?
items.answer: DVC is an open-source tool for data versioning in machine learning projects. It works alongside Git, storing dataset versions in cloud storage while tracking metadata in Git, enabling large dataset versioning without storing full copies in the repository.

items.question: What is the relationship between data versioning and model versioning?
items.answer: Data versioning tracks the data used for training. Model versioning tracks the trained model. They work together — each model version should reference the exact data version it was trained on for full reproducibility.

items.question: Can data versioning be used with streaming data sources?
items.answer: Streaming data presents challenges for versioning because data is continuously arriving. ClickMasters can design approaches that version batches or snapshots of streaming data for training purposes.

items.question: What is data lineage in the context of versioning?
items.answer: Data lineage tracks the origin and transformations of data — where it came from, what preprocessing was applied, and what filtering or augmentation produced each version. It provides full visibility into the data's journey to the training set.
